validated_results.title: Lower serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D is associated with colorectal and breast cancer, but not overall cancer risk: a 20-year cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective community-based cohort measuring baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and reporting incident prostate cancer events over 20 years, with an explicit (null) prostate-cancer risk result.

extraction.comparison_type: Lower (<50 nmol/L) and higher (≥75 nmol/L) serum 25(OH)D versus middle (50-75 nmol/L) group
extraction.population: Community-based adults aged 25 to 84 years at baseline in the Busselton Health Survey

sample_size.excerpt: We hypothesized that serum 25(OH)D was associated with total non-skin cancer incidence and mortality, and/or specifically with colorectal, lung, breast or prostate cancer in an Australian cohort. Serum 25(OH)D was measured in 3818 participants (2166 females) in the 1994/1995 Busselton Health Survey aged 25 to 84 years at baseline.

cases.excerpt: During follow-up (excluding the first 2 years), 212 participants died from non-skin cancer and 634, 110 and 44 participants had non-skin, colorectal and lung cancer events, respectively; 113 women had breast cancer and 122 men had prostate cancer events.

comparison.excerpt: with 28%, 54% and 18% of participants in the lower (<50 nmol/L), middle (50-75 nmol/L) and higher (≥75 nmol/L) vitamin D status groups

timing.excerpt: Cancer mortality and events over 20 years follow-up were determined by data linkage.

validated_results.title: Baseline serum folate, vitamin B12 and the risk of prostate and breast cancer using data from the Swedish AMORIS cohort.
validated_results.reason: Prospective AMORIS cohort of men with baseline serum folate measurements reporting hazard ratios for incident prostate cancer risk categories.

extraction.comparison_type: Serum folate >32 nmol/L versus folate 5-32 nmol/L, for high-risk prostate cancer
extraction.population: Men with serum vitamin B12 and folate measurements in the Swedish AMORIS study

sample_size.excerpt: 8,783 men and 19,775 women with vitamin B12 and folate serum measurements were included.

cases.excerpt: During mean follow-up of 13 years, 703 men developed PCa.

effect_size.excerpt: There was an inverse association between folate > 32 nmol/L and high-risk PCa [hazard ratio (HR) 0.12, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.90], and a positive association between folate < 5 nmol/L and metastatic PCa (HR 5.25, 95% CI 1.29-21.41), compared with folate 5-32 nmol/L.

confidence_interval.excerpt: There was an inverse association between folate > 32 nmol/L and high-risk PCa [hazard ratio (HR) 0.12, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.90], and a positive association between folate < 5 nmol/L and metastatic PCa (HR 5.25, 95% CI 1.29-21.41), compared with folate 5-32 nmol/L.

design.excerpt: We investigated their roles using the prospective Swedish Apolipoprotein MOrtality RISk (AMORIS) study.

continent.excerpt: the prospective Swedish Apolipoprotein MOrtality RISk (AMORIS) study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: 8,783 men and 19,775 women with vitamin B12 and folate serum measurements
